contract: Complete movement frames can follow a pending teleport on the ordered connection. Refused teleports retain the same context and admit those frames. Successful teleports reject old-context frames at authority. Other queued commands and lifecycle requests remain blocked until the teleport reply; sending a movement frame does not clear that barrier. Existing channel, pipeline, interval work, credit, and expiry bounds remain.
regressions: A withheld refused teleport reply no longer prevents the next movement frame from reaching the authority.
A successful teleport rejects the following old-context frame before its reply is released.
Both tests require delivery of both authoritative outcomes and clean worker shutdown.
The pre-send ordered-input regression and post-reply retirement of old-context commands pass.
limitations: Updated native and headless clients and a new persistent delayed 20/40 capture remain required.
Prior barrier evidence remains historical; this change deliberately refines the barrier to allow epoch-checked movement frames.
